correctness.rationale: Finite powerset modal duality identifies the identity \(\Box^3 0=1\) with absence of three-edge walks. A modal congruence ideal is a predecessor-closed set of atoms; in a finite acyclic frame its nonzero ideals have a least member exactly when there is one source. This forces the unique root/middle/terminal partition, nonempty parent subsets and optional root shortcuts. Labeled counting follows by independent choices; unlabeled counting follows by multiset orbits and the fixed-multiset Burnside generating function. A standalone checker exhaustively tested all \(2^{n^2}\) directed relations for \(n=1,2,3,4\) (including cycles/loops), checked all predecessor-closed ideals, graph constructors, automorphism orbits, and exact formulas; it returned VERIFY_OK. This is corroboration, not a proof for arbitrary n.

originality.rationale: The complete primary article by Takahashi (arXiv:2510.14520v1; JSL 2026) identifies finite-height subdirectly irreducible modal algebras as Jankov splitting templates and establishes decidability, without the present intrinsic two-level parent-set classification or exact labeled/unlabeled enumerators. Venema (2002, complete eight-page PDF) proves rootedness/dual characterizations but has no fixed-height census. Searches covering rooted height-two acyclic digraphs, normal modal algebras, labeled counts, Burnside orbits, and sequence tables did not locate a claim implying the present two counting formulas. Public neighboring results count graph maps or different modal properties. An uncataloged graph-enumeration equivalence remains a residual risk; search absence alone is not a proof of originality.

value.rationale: Takahashi/Blok make every finite-height finite subdirectly irreducible modal algebra a natural splitting-template object. Height two is the first layer beyond rooted stars in which nontrivial shared successor incidence and optional transitive shortcuts coexist. The theorem gives a complete, canonical parametrization for every atom size and both labeled and isomorphism-invariant exact counts, enabling duplication-free low-height Jankov template enumeration. It is not merely a bounded computational table or an arbitrary one-off invariant; it identifies the structural degrees of freedom throughout a natural logical class. No claim is made that distinct templates necessarily yield distinct splitting logics.
